title: Space Needle
blurb: Seattle’s 1962 World’s Fair observation tower: 605 ft of Googie-era optimism, three tapering legs carrying a 42 m flying-saucer top house with the observation deck at 520 ft.

sourceUrls.label: Methodshop: How Tall Is the Seattle Space Needle?

systems.name: Foundation and base
systems.description: The 30 ft deep foundation with 72 anchor bolts, the plaza, the ground-level building and the leg footings.

systems.name: Tripod legs
systems.description: The three tapering steel legs that splay at the base, pinch at the waist and flare to carry the top house, tied by cross braces.

systems.name: Central core and elevators
systems.description: The central service core with the stairwell and the three exterior glass elevator shafts.

systems.name: Top house, restaurant level
systems.description: The flying-saucer top house: the restaurant floor at 500 ft with the revolving Loupe glass floor, carried on six struts.

systems.name: Observation level
systems.description: The observation deck at 520 ft with its ring of glass panels, mullions and benches.

systems.name: Roof and halo
systems.description: The conical roof and the red halo ring that crowns the top house.

systems.name: Mast and lightning protection
systems.description: The central mast with 25 lightning rods, the aviation beacon and the flagpole.
